note: Landing sites, landmarks and scenic destinations. Coordinates are Mean Earth/Polar Axis (ME) frame, planetocentric latitude, longitude positive east in -180..180. 'verify' marks rows whose best available source was secondary; see RESEARCH.md.

sites.name: Tranquility Base
sites.blurb: The first place humans stood on another world. Eagle's descent stage is still here, with the seismometer and the laser retroreflector to the south and Little West crater 60 m east.
sites.source: Wagner et al. 2012, ISPRS Archives XXXIX-B4:517 (LROC NAC, ME frame)

sites.name: Apollo 12
sites.blurb: Pinpoint landing 163 m from Surveyor 3, parts of which the crew carried home.

sites.name: Apollo 14
sites.blurb: Fra Mauro highlands: ejecta from the Imbrium basin, and a long uphill walk to Cone crater.

sites.name: Apollo 15
sites.blurb: Between the Apennine mountains and Hadley Rille, a 1.5 km wide lava channel. First rover mission.

sites.name: Apollo 16
sites.blurb: Central highlands, expected to be volcanic and found to be impact breccia instead.

sites.name: Taurus-Littrow
sites.blurb: A deep valley walled by massifs taller than the Grand Canyon is deep, where Schmitt found orange volcanic glass. The last crewed landing.

sites.name: Luna 9
sites.blurb: First survivable landing on another world; returned the first panorama from the surface.

sites.name: Luna 16
sites.blurb: First robotic sample return: 101 g from Mare Fecunditatis.

sites.name: Lunokhod 1
sites.blurb: First wheeled vehicle on another world; drove 10 km. Its retroreflector was relocated by laser ranging in 2010.
sites.source: Murphy et al. 2011 Table 3 (laser ranging, ME frame)

sites.name: Lunokhod 2
sites.blurb: Drove some 39 km across Le Monnier crater, a record that stood for decades.

sites.name: Luna 24
sites.blurb: Last Soviet sample return; found water in the returned core decades later.

sites.name: Surveyor 3
sites.blurb: Visited by Apollo 12 two and a half years later.

sites.name: Surveyor 5
sites.blurb: Slid into a 10 m crater on a 19.7 degree slope and worked anyway.

sites.name: Surveyor 7
sites.blurb: The only Surveyor sent to the highlands, on Tycho's northern ejecta blanket.

sites.name: Chang'e 3
sites.blurb: Mare Imbrium, with the Yutu rover. IAU name: Guang Han Gong.

sites.name: Chang'e 4
sites.blurb: First landing on the far side, inside Von Karman crater in the South Pole-Aitken basin. No direct line of sight to Earth.
sites.source: Liu et al. 2019, Nature Communications (LROC gives -45.4561/177.5885)

sites.name: Chang'e 5
sites.blurb: Sample return from young mare basalt near Mons Ruemker.

sites.name: Chang'e 6
sites.blurb: First sample return from the far side.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram
sites.blurb: Highest-latitude soft landing at the time. IAU name: Statio Shiv Shakti.

sites.name: SLIM
sites.blurb: Landed within 100 m of its target, then tipped onto its nose and survived three lunar nights.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus
sites.blurb: First US soft landing since Apollo; caught a landing leg on a 12 degree slope and toppled.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
sites.blurb: Mare Crisium. Carried the electrodynamic dust shield experiment that finally cleaned lunar dust off a surface in situ.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena
sites.blurb: Came to rest sideways in a 20 m crater near Mons Mouton.

sites.name: ispace Resilience
sites.blurb: Impacted in Mare Frigoris.

sites.name: Tycho
sites.blurb: The youngest big crater on the near side, with a 2 km central peak and the ray system you can see from Earth with the naked eye.

sites.name: Copernicus
sites.blurb: Terraced walls 3.8 km deep, a cluster of central peaks, and a bright ray system across Mare Insularum.

sites.name: Aristarchus
sites.blurb: The brightest large feature on the Moon, on a plateau of volcanic deposits beside Vallis Schroteri.

sites.name: Vallis Schroteri
sites.blurb: The Moon's largest sinuous rille: a collapsed lava channel up to 10 km wide with a smaller channel meandering inside it.

sites.name: Rima Hadley
sites.blurb: Apollo 15 parked at its edge and photographed layered bedrock in the far wall.

sites.name: Mare Imbrium
sites.blurb: The great flooded basin of the near side. Flat, dark and vast: the best driving on the Moon.

sites.name: Mare Orientale
sites.blurb: The youngest and best preserved multi-ring impact basin, three concentric mountain rings around a small dark sea, mostly hidden around the western limb.

sites.name: Tsiolkovskiy
sites.blurb: A dark lava-flooded floor and a bright central peak, unmistakable on the far side. No Earth in this sky.

sites.name: Reiner Gamma
sites.blurb: A bright swirl with no topography at all, painted onto the mare by a magnetic anomaly that deflects the solar wind.

sites.name: Shackleton rim
sites.blurb: Stand on a rim lit about 94% of the lunar year and look down into a floor that has been dark for billions of years. The Sun rolls around the horizon instead of rising.

sites.name: South pole
sites.blurb: Grazing light, kilometre-long shadows, and permanently shadowed floors near 25 K.

sites.name: Mons Malapert
sites.sub: 5 km massif near the south pole
sites.blurb: A high, often sunlit massif with a line of sight to Earth: a perennial candidate for a permanent base.

sites.name: Mons Huygens
sites.blurb: The highest peak on the Moon, in the Apennines on the rim of Imbrium.

sites.name: Marius Hills pit
sites.blurb: A collapse hole about 55 m across opening into what is probably an intact lava tube.

sites.name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
sites.blurb: The deepest known lunar pit: a 100 m hole with an overhanging rim and a boulder-strewn floor.

sites.name: Earth antipode
sites.blurb: The point on the Moon furthest from the Earth, give or take: the antipode of the sub-Earth point, in the far side highlands. The Earth has never risen here and never will. Nudged a fraction off the exact antipode because 0 N 180 E is the seam where longitude changes sign and the point is to stand somewhere, not on a discontinuity.
sites.source: antipode of the mean sub-Earth point; the Moon's synchronous rotation keeps it Earthless

sites.name: South Pole-Aitken basin
sites.sub: ~2500 km, the largest known impact basin
sites.blurb: Eight kilometres deep and older than almost everything else on the Moon; the floor exposes material from the lower crust or mantle.
sites.source: secondary; basin has no IAU centre point
